chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: Kansas City musicianship and Jimmy Blanton; Goodman hears him sing
summary: Turner doesn't know about Blanton but says everyone in Kansas City could play; Goodman heard him sing there.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: It was on one of those trips that he heard Jimmy Blanton, right?

I know that Jimmy Blanton was from St. Louis but I have heard reports that he also played in Kansas City and that that was where Ben Webster first heard him. Do you have any idea if that is true? Blanton would have been just a teenager.
I don't know. Them cats just showed up. They just

come to Kansas City and stayed...'cause that's where it was. Ever'body was blowin' a horn that could blow a horn. We didn't stand for no monkey jive. You had t'be able to play. They was really up-to-date, an' they played music like it was nobody's business.

Benny Goodman heard us on the radio, and he could...brought his band there and he come up. We went up and invited him down...invited his whole band and had barbecue and spaghetti an' everything. And he jus' set and listened...where he heard me sing.
